title: SLO-aware burst mitigator and noise-aware alert routing for usage/cost/latency
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background: Our console alerting pipeline generates a high volume of noisy alerts during short bursts (traffic surges, model rollouts, synthetic tests). This creates alert fatigue for on-call and product owners and obscures true incidents. Existing detectors use static thresholds or simple adaptive windows which either (a) mute legitimate incidents during bursts, or (b) surface too many low-value alerts.

Goal: Implement a SLO-aware burst mitigation layer that reduces false positives during short-lived system noise while preserving detection sensitivity for SLO violations. Add noise-aware routing so alerts are prioritized and routed based on tenant SLA tiers, recent true-positive history, and per-tenant impact scoring. The feature should be compatible with hosted usage/cost/latency pipelines and pluggable into the current console alert router.
acceptance_criteria: Deployable mitigation layer in staging that sits between anomaly detector and alert router and can be toggled per-cluster/namespace
False positive rate for usage/cost/latency alerts reduced by at least 35% on historical burst windows (measured on replay test set) without increasing median detection latency by more than 20%
Per-tenant priority routing correctly applies high-priority channels (pager/email) for customers with enterprise SLA; 95% of high-impact alerts during bursts must still be routed to on-call
Provide a Console dashboard panel showing suppressed alert counts, suppression reasons, and mitigation score distribution
Runbook and automated playbook created for mitigation-induced alert suppression and manual override available via Console (can un-suppress a series by tenant/time window)
End-to-end e2e tests cover canonical scenarios: short synthetic spike, sustained degradation, model rollout-induced spike
Canary rollout to 10% of traffic with metrics monitoring and automated rollback on regressions (regression = FP increase >10% or missed SLO >5%)
technical_notes: High-level approach: Introduce a scoring function that combines: detector confidence, burstiness factor (derived from short-window z-score), tenant impact weight, and recent true-positive rate to compute mitigation score
Mitigation states: allow, delay (hold for X seconds and re-evaluate after aggregation), suppress (drop but log), and escalate (force through) based on score thresholds configurable per-release/tenant
Storage: short-lived suppression windows stored in Redis cluster with TTLs; long-term audit events persisted to events-store for forensics
Tuning: implement offline replay harness to sweep scoring coefficients against labeled historical windows; store best candidate coefficients in feature flags for canary experiments

Compatibility: keep existing detector outputs unchanged; mitigation layer subscribes to detector pub/sub topic and emits augmented alerts to router topic; provide a compatibility shim for legacy consumers
Observability: instrument suppression decisions with reason codes and tags (tenant_id, detector_id, score_components) for per-token cost/latency correlation in Console
Security/Privacy: suppressed payloads still need to obey PII rules — redact payloads before audit persistence; security review required for persistence schema changes
